reasoning: Thirty-second operation and five-second cleanup timers are fixed internal policy. Success still requires zero-code close, bounded output and no latched failure; observed exit alone cannot resolve success.

Timeout, overflow, stdin/stdout/stderr/child failures latch failure before a single owned ChildProcess kill request. Reentrant/late events see the latch. No signal is sent through a numeric PID or unrelated process handle. Kill return value is not treated as proof of termination.

On failure, observed exit or close permits generic rejection and disposal of owned streams. Synchronous spawn throw and asynchronous error without a PID are sanitized and do not invent an existing child or retain a pointless mutation lock.

After cleanup grace with no observed termination, only owned streams are disposed and owned child unreferenced. A module-private WeakSet marker causes mutate to close its file handle but retain state.lock. Later events cannot silently release that quarantined admission lock. No exported test seam or public marker exists.

Protect failure reaches mutate before any credential/config write. Unprotect failure maps to the existing generic REMOTE_CREDENTIAL boundary and preserves files. The underlying credential binding, CurrentUser DPAPI, fixed entropy, fixed command script, stdin-only secret transport and 32768-byte output ceiling remain unchanged.

The new test file runs sequentially in an isolated test process, invokes actual RemoteStateStore with fixture directories, and substitutes builtin spawn/platform/timers only for each test. Existing platform-native roundtrip tests remain present. Deterministic fake children prove the state machine, not actual DPAPI cryptography or OS termination.

Installed verifier imports the installed module from the isolated prefix after matching exact pre-pack remote module bytes, then exercises synthetic savePairing/credential/clearPairing. It explicitly reports actualRemoteEnrollment:false, realUserStateAccessed:false, modelCalls:0, and Windows-only fields as null on POSIX.

Successful installed Protect and Unprotect require close observed when the store operation settles. Missing-executable attempts are separately required to have ENOENT, no PID and no exit observation. The verifier never prints raw token, ciphertext, child streams or unexpected error text.
